lines: Vantry: Psst. Wayfarer. You look honest. Shame, but I'll work with it.
Vantry: The Quiet Hands broke into my cellar and nicked my stock. Hush jars. Voices in bottles. Very legal. Mostly.
Vantry: Clear them out and we split the take. Sixty-forty. Me sixty. It's my cellar, sweetheart.
Vantry: Still here? The door's right there. Mind the stairs, they bite.
The pawnshop is boarded up. A note: 'Gone fishing. Forever. Don't look for me. - V.'
Snib: Oi! Shop's shut. Permanently. Like your mouth's about to be.
Snib: Ow. Fine. The boss is downstairs. She bites harder than the stairs.
Snib: I'm on my break. Being beaten counts as a break.
Tull: Vantry sent you? Course he did. He sends someone every week.
Tull: You're better than last week's. Last week's cried.
Tull: Ask yourself why a pawnbroker has a key to his own robbers' den.
Mopsy: This is the counting room. You're not on the count.
Mopsy: Recount! Recount!
Mopsy: Every jar down here has a voice in it. Some of them still swear.
Ledge: One more step and I tell Mother. She hates being told things.
Ledge: Mother's going to hate this.
Ledge: Go on, then. She's through there. I'll be over here, not helping.
Skiv: Last guard before the office. I'm paid double for this door.
Skiv: Double of nothing. I should read contracts.
Skiv: She knew you were coming. Someone told her. Guess who.
Mother Crowle: Vantry's little errand runner. Sit. No? Fine, stand and lose.
Mother Crowle: This is his cellar, sweetheart. These are his jars. We're his staff.
Mother Crowle: He sent you down because you're cheaper than a locksmith and easier to blame.
Mother Crowle: Fine. Take the ledger. Read page three.
Mother Crowle: Your name's on it. He sold you to us for forty coins. Forty! I'd have paid fifty.
You open the jars. Voices drift up the stairs and out into Thornridge, grumbling.
Mother Crowle: Vantry's gone, isn't he? Course he is. Trust no one, sweetheart. Especially me.
Jinks: Oi, lighthouse kid! Jinks Calloway. Remember it, I'll be famous by Tuesday.
Jinks: Kestra's new pet, yeah? Let's see if you bite.
Jinks: Lucky. Proper lucky. I'll be ahead of you on the next path, watch.
Jinks: Ha! Go home, the lamp needs dusting.
Jinks: Took your time. I've been up here an hour freezing my mouth off.
Jinks: Funny thing. Someone pays me to slow you down. Good money. Nothing personal.
Jinks: Right. Fine. That's two. Don't tell anyone, I've got a rep.
Jinks: Told you. Ahead of you. Always.
Jinks: Last round, lighthouse. Win and I tell you who's paying me. Or I lie. Depends how hard you hit.
Jinks: Ugh. Deal's a deal.
Jinks: It's Vantry. The pawnbroker. Pays per day you're late. Says you'll owe him one day and he wants you skint.
Jinks: Also I sold him your route. And your favourite snack. Sorry. Slow week.
Jinks: Not today, lighthouse. Today I'm rich.
Gnasher thrashes off into the lake, line and all.
The water goes still. Your coins go with it.
Tobin: Take a coat. Take two. Just don't take me to Gisk.
Tobin: Nice coat. Mine now.
Granny Reed: It IS tonic. Tonic for frogs.
Granny Reed: Have a sip, love. On the house.
Fabbro: My brother posted this? Of course. He wants my half of the shop. He wrote the bounty on my good paper.
Fabbro: Tell my brother the shop's still half mine. The worse half.
The cheap end of the board. Small fry, small pay.

lines: Gisk: Bounties! Fresh bounties! Every one a villain, every one paid in coin. Terms and conditions apply.

lines: The board is empty. Someone has drawn a little crown on it.
Soot Mag: I only took the warm bits!
Soot Mag: Now you're the one covered in soot.
The Hush Hound lets out one tiny bark and slinks away.
The Hush Hound does not even bark. That's worse.
Rattle Jim: I foresaw this. I foresee everything. Wrongly.
Rattle Jim: I foresaw you losing. First time I've been right!
Brannagh: You read the small print. Nobody reads the small print. Yes, it's me. I posted myself to collect my own reward. Twice.
Brannagh: Not a word. I'll pay you from my own reward. Which is your reward. It's complicated.

lines: Brannagh: Thornridge bounty board. Read it, fight it, get paid. Nobody ever reads the small print.

lines: The board is empty. Someone has drawn a little crown on it.
Brennick: Three folk owe me. Hobb in Fernstair, Marl in Crowcrest, Nettie in Quillbrook.
Brennick: Collect, and you keep a tenth. Generous, I know. I cried writing it.
Brennick: Hobb, Marl, Nettie. Three names, three receipts. Chop chop.
Brennick: Well? Where's my money?

choices.text: Show him the three receipts.
Say nothing and take your tenth.

lines: Brennick: Receipts? Oh, these. Funny how paper burns.
Brennick: Nobody calls me a cheat in my own village. Not without a fight.
Brennick: Fine! Debts cancelled. All of them. I'll start new ones tomorrow.
Brennick: That'll be ten coins for the lesson. Plus interest.
Brennick: Your tenth. In tonics. Coin's tight.
Brennick: And between us, I sold your name to a collector in Corvane. Business is business, pet.
Brennick: Need a loan? Low rates. Lower than yesterday. Higher than tomorrow.
Hobb: Owe him? I paid Brennick twice. He loses the receipts on purpose.
Hobb: Here, have a copy of mine. A copy, mind. He eats originals.
Marl: I borrowed ten coins in spring. Now I owe four hundred. The interest has interest. It's breeding.
Marl: Take the receipt. Burn it, frame it, I don't care.
Nettie: Brennick sent you? You're the third collector this month. The other two work for me now.
Nettie: Here's my receipt. Show him. Watch his face. Better than theatre.
Hobb: Brennick? Don't say that name near my ferns. They wilt.
Marl: If anyone asks, I'm not here. I'm a rock. Rocks don't owe money.
Nettie: Quillbrook runs on gossip and ducks. Mostly gossip.
Nettle: Run a parcel to Watchman Corr in Crowcrest. Don't open it. Don't shake it. Don't let it hear you talk about the Hush.
Nettle: Easy money, love. Easiest you'll ever make.
Nettle: Parcel's not going to deliver itself, love. Well. It might. Don't let it.
Nettle: You're walking around free? Huh. Corr's slipping. No hard feelings, love. Business.
Corr: A parcel from Nettle? For me? How thoughtful.
Corr: It's a jar of stolen voices. With your fingerprints all over it. Nettle sends me a fresh fool every month. You're this month's.
Corr: Off the record: beat my Spirlings and the paperwork gets lost.
Corr: Move along. Nothing to see. Especially not in my pockets.
Corr: Paperwork's lost. Tell Nettle she owes me a new fool.
Corr: I'll file this under 'pending'. Come back when you're less guilty.
Mrs Gristle: My poor Shalebat Pebble has passed on. Tragic. Sudden. Very well insured.
Mrs Gristle: The Wardens' fund pays for lost Spirlings. I just need a witness. Sign here? Little scribble?
Mrs Gristle: Still grieving. Very loudly. In case the fund is listening.
Mrs Gristle: You went to Murk Hollow? Why would anyone go to Murk Hollow?

choices.text: Keep her secret and take a cut.
Tell her the fund will hear of it.

lines: Mrs Gristle: Smart child. Here's your share. If anyone asks, Pebble's a ghost now.
Mrs Gristle: Then I'll have to bury two of us. Figuratively. Mostly.
Mrs Gristle: Pebble has been resurrected. A miracle. The fund wants its money back. Miracles are expensive.
Mrs Gristle: Two funerals in one week. I'll get a discount.
Mrs Gristle: Pebble sends his love. From beyond. Beyond the hill, specifically.
A plump Shalebat hangs here, very much alive, chewing a sandwich wrapped in Mrs Gristle's best napkin.
A plump Shalebat hangs here, chewing. It glares at you like you owe it rent.

Wicka: Hush coins, dearie. Stamped with a closed mouth. Eight of them lie about Veydal.
Wicka: Bring me all eight and I pay proper. No questions. I hate questions.
Wicka: Eight coins, dearie. Not seven. Seven is a sad number.
Wicka: All eight! Lovely. Here's your pay.
Wicka: Between us, I minted them myself and hid them. Best treasure hunt I ever sold. Forty Wayfarers did it this year.
Wicka: Hide them again tomorrow, I will. Don't tell the next one.
